title: Would I still trust Toyota and Lexus after this massive recall? - USA Today

 Does this latest recall make Toyota and Lexus vehicles unreliable?
 Charles Singh USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 12:54 p.m. ET Hear this story Toyota and Lexus are recalling over 314,000 vehicles due to faulty Takata airbag inflators.
 The defective inflators can rupture and send metal fragments into the vehicle's cabin.
 Affected models include several Toyota and Lexus nameplates, primarily from older model years.
 Toyota and its luxury division Lexus are issuing a massive recall on 314,029 models over an issue with Takata airbag inflators. The Japanese car brand is known for its reliability and the popularity of affordable nameplates.
 Its Lexus models have also become extremely popular in luxury vehicle segments because of their value and strong build quality. Does the airbag recall bring Toyota and Lexus' dependability into question?
 The answer is more complicated than you may think.
 Why are Toyota and Lexus cars being recalled?
 Toyota and Lexus models are being recalled because defective Takata airbag inflators can send metal fragments into the cabin if they're ruptured. The recall extends to three Lexus nameplates and four Toyota nameplates so far.
 Toyota/Lexus models being recalled over Takata airbags
 Lexus IS (2011)
 Lexus GX (2017)
 Lexus SC (2002-2010)
 Toyota Corolla (2003-2008)
 Toyota 4Runner (2016-2017)
 Toyota Tundra (2005-2006)
 Toyota Sequoia (2005-2007)
 Owners should contact their local Toyota or Lexus service centers as soon as possible to schedule their free repairs. Dealers will completely replace the airbag or inflator to remedy this issue.

Here's why Want to test a car for days before buying it? Here's one way you can What's new with the 2027 Toyota Tundra, and would I recommend it? Are Takata airbags a major cause for concern?
 Takata supplies most automotive brands with airbags including Honda, Toyota, Nissan, Ford, Chevrolet, BMW, Mercedes-Benz are more. Around 67 million Takata airbags were recalled in waves from 2008 to 2020, so Toyota's recent recall isn't a new issue for the automotive industry.
 Takata airbags are a cause for concern, but so many popular automotive brands and vehicles utilize their airbags that they would be difficult to avoid entirely. If you own a vehicle that's part of a recall, take it in for service as soon as possible to avoid airbag-related injuries.
 Are Toyota and Lexus cars reliable?
 Toyota produces some of the longest-lasting cars on the market including models like the Sequoia, 4Runner , Tundra and Tacoma according to a study by iSeeCars.com . Toyota models tend to be dependable over long ownership periods and have a high likelihood of outlasting rivals.
 While the Takata airbag recall is concerning, it shouldn't directly impact Toyota's reputation for producing dependable vehicles since Takata airbags are so common. It's also important to note that the recall mainly impacts older model years (up to 2017) instead of more recent models.
 Why I would still consider Toyota and Lexus cars following the recall
 I've tested around 30 brand-new cars in 2026 including sports cars, trucks SUVs, transit vans and even an autonomous vehicle. Toyota is one of my favorite car brands because their vehicles offer strong value and longevity at affordable prices. Models like the Corolla and Tacoma are staples in their segments.
 The Takata airbag recall doesn't make Toyota and Lexus vehicles inherently unreliable, but these issues should be taken seriously and addressed quickly.
